question: A car travels (1)/(3) of the distance on a straight road at a speed of 10 km/h, the next (1)/(3) at a speed of 20 km/h and the last (1)/(3) at a speed of 60 km/h. Find the average speed of the car.
solution:
**Given:**

1/3 distance at 10 km/h, 1/3 distance at 20 km/h, 1/3 distance at 60 km/h.

**Concept:**

The average speed is total distance divided by total time.

**Solution:**

Time taken in first part of journey = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time1 = (D/3) / 10

Time taken in second part of journey = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time2 = (D/3) / 20

Time taken in last part of journey = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time3 = (D/3) / 60

Total time taken for the entire journey = Sum of time taken in all parts

⇒ Total Time = Time1 + Time2 + Time3

Total Distance covered in the journey = D

Substitute values from steps 1-4 in the formula for average speed:

⇒ Average Speed = D / Total Time

Average Speed = D / [ (D/3)/10 + (D/3)/20 + (D/3)/60 ]

By simplifying above equation,

Average Speed = D / [ (D/30) + (D/60) + (D/180) ]

Average Speed = D / [ (6D + 3D + D) / 180 ]

Average Speed = 180 / 10

**Hence, the average speed of the car is 18 km/h.**
